solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: More than one outdoor market carries beers hiding short volume

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its tail, so the final letter is dropped
whatever hides something keeps it tucked away inside, so one run of letters goes within another

parts.note: to cart something is to carry it
a volume is a BOOK, trimmed of its last letter
ales are beers

explanation.surface: A street market is doing a brisk trade in beer, with a shortage of books on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: A car-boot sale is a British market where people sell unwanted goods from the backs of their cars. The deletion happens first, then the shortened word is tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Car-boot sales are informal open-air markets held in fields or car parks, so the plural covers several such events.

clue.text: Where one might sing anthem's opening line

parts.note: an opening is an opportunity or chance
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A choir member asks about the first words of the anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening line' reads as one phrase about the anthem, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar where the choir traditionally sits and performs.

clue.text: Baker perhaps chasing rodent: something toothy

indicators.note: a chaser comes behind what it pursues, so this piece is placed after the other

parts.note: a rat is a rodent
Chet Baker was an American jazz trumpeter, so Baker is one example of someone called Chet

explanation.surface: A baker, or perhaps a dog, chases a rodent and bares its teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Baker looks like a person who bakes; it is the surname of jazz musician Chet Baker, and 'perhaps' flags that it gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed wheel or bar engaged by a pawl, so it is a mechanism literally covered in teeth.

clue.text: Working, approach Emergency Room about temperature measurement device

indicators.note: to be about something is to be around it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
to approach is to come near
ER is the abbreviation for emergency room
T is the symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: A medic on duty is asked to bring a thermometer to casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temperature measurement device' looks like one phrase meaning thermometer, but temperature belongs to the wordplay. Here the hospital abbreviation and the approach word together wrap round the temperature letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oncometer is an instrument for recording variations in the volume of an organ, so it is a kind of gauge.

clue.text: Fizzy drink tons mostly kept ready

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tons
something on ice is kept in reserve, ready for use; lose its last letter

explanation.surface: Crates of soft drinks are mostly stored ready for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tons mostly' looks like TON, but 'mostly' shortens ON ICE, the idiom for being held in reserve, and tons is only T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a carbonated mixer flavoured with quinine, served with gin.

clue.text: Overwhelm a small Scots settlement with 500

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
toun is the Scots spelling of town
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Five hundred incomers flood a tiny Scottish village.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUN is a Scots dialect word for a town or farmstead.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound someone is to amaze them so greatly that they are overcome with surprise.

clue.text: Train from east expected outside Bombay, perhaps

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: a train that is expected is due
the Bombay is a breed of black domestic cat

explanation.surface: A railway announcement: the service from the east is due outside Mumbai.
explanation.walkthrough: Train, east, expected and Bombay all build an Indian railway scene, but train is a verb and Bombay is a breed of cat, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach or instruct them, the same sense as educating them.

clue.text: Took a quiet stay — I settled into valued surroundings

parts.note: taken as written
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a stay is a support or prop

indicators.note: to settle into a place is to come to rest within it, so one letter goes inside another word
surroundings enclose what sits in them, confirming which word forms the outer shell

parts.note: something valued has been rated
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone enjoyed a peaceful holiday in pleasant, well-regarded surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: Stay looks like a visit or holiday, but it is a noun for a support, as in the stays of a mast. Quiet is P from musical notation.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it for one's own use, often without permission.

clue.text: Means of payment most recently in Indian currency, not English

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is enclosed by it
saying something is not there removes it, and English stands for its abbreviated letter

parts.note: the pice was a small Indian coin, a quarter of an anna
what happened most recently happened last

explanation.surface: A traveller in India asks which recent currency to use.
explanation.walkthrough: The pice is an obsolete coin, so few solvers will think of it; the English letter comes off its end after the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is informal slang for credit and debit cards, which are used to pay instead of cash.

clue.text: Top bid — never the bottom

parts.note: never is a strong not
the rump is the backside or bottom

explanation.surface: An auction slogan: bid high, never go in at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen falls after NO, but the wordplay splits the letters after the T. The bid belongs to the card game bridge, not an auction room.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a contract without a trump suit ranks above all others at each level, making it the highest call.

clue.text: All the papers united over revolting process of coercion

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a gerund

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
those revolting are staging a rising or rebellion

explanation.surface: The whole press joins forces against a disgusting campaign of bullying.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting looks like an adjective meaning disgusting; here it means rebelling. In a down clue 'over' simply places one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressurising someone means applying strong persuasion or pressure to make them act, which is a form of coercion.

clue.text: Frame horse by a male illustrator

parts.note: a rack is a framework for holding things
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A framed picture of a horse by a male artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse for H goes via its drug-slang sense, heroin. Arthur Rackham was an English illustrator of fairy tales and children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Rackham is famous for his early twentieth-century drawings for Peter Pan and Grimm's tales.

clue.text: Stomach time when Henry's missing in prison

indicators.note: being in a place means enclosed by it

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement

indicators.note: something missing has gone, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: an hour is a period of time
H is the SI unit symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A prisoner doing time loses his appetite when his friend Henry is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Stomach looks like a body part or a verb; it is a noun meaning nerve. Henry is the physics unit of inductance, whose symbol is a single capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have the stomach for something is to have the nerve or bravery it demands.

clue.text: Guide map includes capital of India

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: to map out a route is to plot it

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its capital letter, the first one

parts.note: the opening letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: A tourist guide's map marks New Delhi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of India' wants to be Delhi, but it only means the first letter of India.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot something is to steer or direct it, the same sense as guiding it.

clue.text: Spread dissent about record lack of enthusiasm

indicators.note: being about something means lying around it
things spread out are scattered from their original order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Opposition spreads over a recording that nobody is excited about.
explanation.walkthrough: Dissent is a verb in the surface but simply supplies seven letters to jumble; the record is the short extended-play kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid literally means lukewarm, and figuratively describes a half-hearted, unenthusiastic reaction.

clue.text: Go for a revolutionary number one sausage

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, which is pep
per means for each or a, as in ten pounds per hour

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to back a revolutionary leader, number one in the movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' is not a single idea: only the number is turned round, and the one follows it. Go is a noun meaning energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy Italian-American cured salami, often sliced onto pizza.

clue.text: Unusual tip re corn: grow in alternating rows

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A farming column offers an odd piece of advice about maize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip re corn' reads as an agricultural hint, which suits the definition while supplying all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Intercropping is the farming practice of raising two crops together, often in alternate strips on one field.

clue.text: Land for cultivation I get all prepared

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up or worked into shape, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer boasts of readying every field for planting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the definition so well that 'prepared' seems part of the farming picture rather than an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is ground that is ploughed and tilled for growing crops, as well as the act of tilling it.

clue.text: Piece of ginger? Initially rare one unknown among roots?

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

indicators.note: things among others sit in their midst, so these letters go inside

parts.note: one's roots are where one comes from, one's home
I is the Roman numeral for one
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A redhead's rare origins are traced back through the family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Ginger looks like a red-haired person; it is the spice plant. Roots means where one comes from, not plant roots, despite the ginger.
explanation.definitionFit: Root ginger is botanically an underground stem, a rhizome, so a knob of it is a portion of one; the question mark flags that.

clue.text: Time to abandon beer, one included with the champers?

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter drops out

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Time to give up the beer and join the celebration with champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne, which the beer encourages you to read; here it means those who champ, or chew. BITTER loses one T.
explanation.definitionFit: Champing means biting or munching noisily, so anything that bites belongs among champers; the question mark marks the invented noun.

clue.text: Early car company's enthusiasm at rising appeal

parts.note: a bug is a craze or enthusiasm, as in the travel bug
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A vintage carmaker's eagerness to broaden its market.
explanation.walkthrough: Appeal for IT is a crossword favourite, from the 1920s use of 'it' for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugatti was founded in 1909 in Alsace and built famous racing and luxury cars in the interwar years.

clue.text: Bard's lover Romeo, one mixing with louts

indicators.note: things mixing together are stirred up, so all the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Romeo falls in with a gang of yobs.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is the obvious Shakespearean lover and seems to be the answer, but it only gives R. The Bard is Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Troilus is the Trojan prince who loves Cressida in Shakespeare's play Troilus and Cressida.

clue.text: Composer penning key scores

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, as sheep in a pen

parts.note: Thomas Tallis was an English Tudor composer
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A composer is writing music in a particular key.
explanation.walkthrough: Penning and scores both suggest writing music, but penning means enclosing and scores are totals.
explanation.definitionFit: A tally is a running count or total, and a score is likewise the count of points in a game.

clue.text: Likely loner unpaired since turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning upward means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: an unpaired sock is an odd one
as can mean since, as in 'as it was late'

explanation.surface: Someone single since arriving is probably a solitary type.
explanation.walkthrough: Saddo is British slang for a pathetic, socially inept person.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddo is someone considered boring and friendless, so such a person is probably often on their own.

clue.text: Nut by net's opposite rivet

parts.note: in printing, an en space is called a nut
gross is the reverse of net, as in pay before or after deductions

explanation.surface: A hardware list: nut, net and rivet read like fixings.
explanation.walkthrough: Nut and rivet belong together in a toolbox, but rivet is a verb meaning hold attention and nut is printers' jargon for an en.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rivets you absorbs your whole attention, just as an engrossing book does.

clue.text: Stone for engagement day no girl's sent back

indicators.note: whatever is sent back returns the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day
taken as written
a maid is a girl

explanation.surface: On the day of the engagement, the girl says no and returns the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: All three pieces are turned round together as one string, not each on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds are the traditional gems set in engagement rings.

clue.text: Bird returning in autumn, a lot roosting

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters are read backwards
a word lying in a phrase is buried within its letters

parts.note: read backwards from the end of the first word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: Migrant birds come back in the autumn and many settle to roost.
explanation.walkthrough: Returning suits migrating birds, which disguises its role as the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European bunting, notorious as a French delicacy.

clue.text: During awful siege appeal follows emperor's liberal acts

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so one piece sits inside another
something awful is in a terrible state, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: what follows comes after, fixing the order of two pieces

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: During a dreadful siege, an emperor answers a plea with acts of mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: Appeal is IT, as in 1920s slang for sex appeal. The emperor and the appeal join first, then the jumbled siege letters wrap round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean open-handed and bountiful, so liberal acts are instances of giving freely.
